cards.explanation: The answer is their faith in the Lord Jesus and their love for all the saints. That's the news that reached Paul, friends: "…your faith in the Lord Jesus and your love for all the saints…" (Ephesians 1:15). Faith in Jesus and love for God's people, both in one sentence. I think that's the kind of report that makes a person grab a pencil and start a prayer list.

The answer is in their knowledge of Him. Paul prays for "…a spirit of wisdom and revelation in your knowledge of Him." (Ephesians 1:17). The wisdom is about knowing God Himself, friends. He's asking the glorious Father to give it, and that's the whole point.

The answer is False. Paul prays for "…the eyes of your heart…" to be enlightened (Ephesians 1:18), not for anyone's eyes to be healed. Nothing in the text talks about eyesight here, friends. He wants them to know something, and he says what in the next verses.

The answer is the hope of His calling and the greatness of His power. Paul names "the hope of His calling, the riches of His glorious inheritance in the saints, and the surpassing greatness of His power to us who believe" (Ephesians 1:18-19). That's three things, friends, and the hope and the power are both in there. That's a lot of knowing packed into one prayer.

The answer is that He raised Him from the dead and seated Him at His right hand. God's mighty strength was exerted in Christ "…when He raised Him from the dead and seated Him at His right hand in the heavenly realms…" (Ephesians 1:20). Raised and seated, both in one verse, friends. That's strength I can't even bake a joke about.

The answer is True. Christ is seated "…far above all rule and authority, power and dominion, and every name that is named, not only in the present age but also in the one to come." (Ephesians 1:21). Right now and the age to come, both covered, friends. Paul says it reaches into both.

The answer is His body. Christ is head over everything for the church, "…which is His body…" (Ephesians 1:22-23). Head and body, right there together in one breath, friends. I think that's a picture worth chewing on slowly.
